# Adesh Gairola

> Founder of raxIT Labs. AI security company working two directions, with one as primary: security for AI (governance, threat modeling, runtime guardrails for AI products) as the main focus, and AI for security (using AI to automate threat modeling, detection, and compliance work) as the unusual sideline. Open-source releases alongside the platform (model-scanner, GrayZoneBench, mcp-oauth-sample, DirePhish). Sydney, Australia. 15+ years putting security between systems that move fast and things that can't break. Network → Cloud → AI. Ex-AWS Security. Tagline: "Security is a habit, not a project."

## What I do

- Founder & CEO, raxIT Labs. Security for AI as the primary work (governance, threat modeling, runtime guardrails for AI products); AI for security as the unusual sideline (using AI to automate threat modeling, detection, and compliance work). Independent labs releasing open-source security tooling alongside the platform.
- Speaker, AI Engineer Melbourne 2026. Talk: "Kill the God Agent" (autonomous-agent threat modeling), June 3–4
- OWASP LLM Top 10 contributor

## Selected work

- AWS ANZ AI Security Consulting Practice: built and led the regional AI Security consulting practice inside AWS Professional Services. 150+ enterprise engagements across financial services, government, resources, telecom, and professional services (Tier-1 Australian banks, mining majors, NZ government). Apr 2023 – Dec 2025.
- AWS Threat Composer (AI threat-modeling framework): co-authored STRIDE + MAESTRO framework adopted by AWS teams 2024–2025. Productised in AWS Threat Composer.
- AWS Control Tower Proactive Controls: project-led the engineering rollout of native CloudFormation Hooks-based proactive controls deployed across the AWS customer fleet.
- Multi-modal content moderation for ANZ enterprise GenAI: adopted by Tier-1 Australian banks for centralized internal GenAI platforms under APRA CPS 234.
- model-scanner (open source): Apache 2.0 Claude Code skill. Scans ML model files, scores risk 0–100, maps to OWASP LLM Top 10 and Australian ISM-2072. https://github.com/raxITlabs/skills
- GrayZoneBench (open source): Apache 2.0 AI safety benchmark for frontier-model gray-zone requests. https://github.com/raxITlabs/GrayZoneBench
- mcp-oauth-sample (open source): OAuth 2.1 + MCP server reference implementation on Vercel. https://github.com/raxITlabs/mcp-oauth-sample
- DirePhish (open source): AGPL AI-agent red-team simulator and IR-tabletop engine. Clones your team into agents, drops a threat actor into Slack and email, runs the breach 100 times under regulatory time-bounds. https://github.com/raxITlabs/DirePhish
- crucible (open source): Configurable enterprise simulation engine. Multi-agent simulation primitive in Python. https://github.com/raxITlabs/crucible
- securing-ralph-loop (open source): Security checks for the Ralph coding-agent loop. Scan before commit, fix iteratively, escalate when stuck. A practical example of the AI-for-security direction. https://github.com/agairola/securing-ralph-loop

## Featured

Curated highlights pointing to canonical sources. Three things worth your time right now: a long-form essay, a product, and an open-source release.

- [TRUST ME BRO is not a security control](https://raxitlabs.com/blogs/claude-47-five-layers-cyber-blocking): The trust boundary moved inside the model. Three zones, five layers of controls Anthropic ships before your prompt hits the API. April 2026.
- [DirePhish](https://raxitlabs.com/labs/direphish): AI clones of your team running 100 simulated breaches under regulatory time-bounds. A distribution of how you actually behave when the binder goes out the window. April 2026.
- [securing-ralph-loop](https://github.com/agairola/securing-ralph-loop): Security checks bolted into the Ralph coding-agent loop. Scan before commit, fix iteratively, escalate when stuck. The AI-for-security thesis as code.

## How I think

- Business first. Security in service of the outcome the business wants.
- First principles. Start from the problem, not the checklist.
- Practitioner-first. 150+ audits. Tools shipped. Regulation translated into code, not slides.
- Pattern recognition. Same problems, different scales. Name the pattern.
- Paranoia as compass. The thing that makes me uncomfortable is usually the thing worth building for.
- Think Big. Small bets are a tax on time.
